doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bird, Coltrane and Dinah Washington recollections
title: Coltrane, Sonny Rollins and others who could invent
summary: Cobb talks about Cannonball, Trane and Miles; Miles used Trane to answer Rollins.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Any other musician you worked with that you felt was at that level of capacity to invent, just like that?
Julian was like that. Trane. All them guys. Miles.
In the same way? Because it seemed like Trane got to it differently.

He got to it differently, because he had to have something different, because at one time Miles had two tenor players. He had Sonny Rollins and Trane. He would just get them up there and see what they was going to do to each other. For a long time, Sonny Rollins a saxophone colossus. Everybody in the world wanted to play like Sonny Rollins. In fact, you can hear – you can probably still hear it now, that influence that he had on the tenor players, most of them. So every night he used to get up there, and Sonny used to tear him up. So he said, oh, I’m getting tired of this whipping. Said, I got to figure out something else to do here to get across this. So he got to working on what he was working on. He went in – and I think, in the end, it confused Sonny, because Sonny didn’t know what it was.
Did Trane always have the sound and have to develop the concept? Or, did . . . ?

Trane went through a lot of phases. Trane, I told you, was with Earl Bostic. He had to play that way. He had to play the blues. He went through all of these kind of things. First – Trane started out playing the alto saxophone. Then he heard Charlie Parker and said, no, this is not it. This is not going to be it.
